title: Durable lane write lease
description: The compare-and-swap record that decides which run may write which paths, and the reason concurrent mutation by two lanes is structurally impossible rather than merely discouraged. It is a record of its own in its own file, written beside the status artifact it protects and never inside it, for two reasons: it binds that artifact by filesystem identity, and no record can bind the file it lives in; and the two must be able to fail independently, since a lane can legitimately hold a status artifact with no live lease. The binding runs one way — the lease names the artifact, the artifact holds no reference to the lease.

schema.description: Schema name and version of this record.

lease_state.description: Carried on the lease itself, so a released lease is a recorded fact rather than something inferred from a missing file. The active-lane claim mirrors this value and the lease stays the authority if the two disagree.

channel_scope_id.description: The conversation surface this lease belongs to.

origin_message_id.description: The inbound message the lease's lane was opened for.

root_run_id.description: The durable run that owns the lease.

child_session_key.description: The isolated child session the owning run executes in. Carried alongside the run id so a mismatch in either one is detectable. Identity is never repaired in place: a mismatch is reported, never corrected, because a wrong guess silently transfers ownership of live work.

generation.description: Monotonic counter of ownership handovers. A stale holder's write is rejected by its number alone. Taking the lease from a dead owner requires generation N plus one together with a successor record; a same-run resume leaves it unchanged and is idempotent.

epoch.description: Monotonic counter of the lease's own versions. A writer reads the current value and its write succeeds only if the stored value is still the one it read; if another writer got there first the acquire fails instead of overwriting.

protects_status_artifact.description: The status artifact this lease guards, named by filesystem identity and not only by path, so a file deleted and recreated at the same path is correctly seen as a different file. This binding is the reason the lease is a separate record: nested inside the artifact it would be copied along with any replacement and would then certify the replacement as the file it was guarding.

runtime_owner.description: Which live runtime holds the lease, and when it last proved it was alive.

provider_authenticated.description: Whether the holding runtime can still reach the delivery route. A holder that cannot deliver cannot discharge the obligation its lane owes.

locked_write_sets.description: The concrete sets of paths the owning worker may modify. Each is additionally guarded by an exclusive lock file, so a second writer fails to acquire rather than interleaving. A colliding acquire performs no writes at all and returns a typed collision, which becomes exactly one deduplicated blocker.

real_path.description: The resolved path, so two names for one location cannot be leased twice.

reacquired.description: Marker recording that a resume reacquired this lease idempotently under the same run, which changes nothing and is therefore safe to repeat.

successor_record.description: Present only when ownership was taken from a dead owner. Absent for a same-run resume, because nothing changed hands.

inventory_diff.description: What the dead owner left behind.

fan_in_plan.description: How that residue will be reconciled. A takeover with no plan for the previous owner's partial work is a second writer with extra steps.
